author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Oak Bluffs police are investigating a reported sexual assault at the Massachusetts State Police barracks on Martha’s Vineyard and have executed court-authorized search warrants at the facility.

The local department received the report in August, according to statements reported Thursday by NBC 10. Massachusetts State Police said the allegation involves two people who are not affiliated with the department. Authorities have not publicly identified either person or announced criminal charges.

Oak Bluffs Police Chief Jonathan Searle said his department has handled the case independently from State Police and followed its established investigative procedures. State Police said the agency is cooperating with the local inquiry and remains committed to pursuing justice in sexual-assault cases.

Oak Bluffs investigators are working with the Cape and Islands District Attorney’s Office. The agencies did not disclose what was sought or collected under the warrants, and the report did not describe the circumstances of the alleged assault. The inquiry remains active, meaning the reported allegation has not been tested in court. Officials have not announced a timetable for further information.
dek: Local officers executed court-authorized warrants at the Martha’s Vineyard facility while investigating an August report involving two people unaffiliated with State Police.
headline: Oak Bluffs police search state barracks in sexual-assault investigation
